lost_bodies._data_status_note: No public register of Nagpur's lost lakes has been found, so none can be placed in wards.

flood._data_status_note: NMC's City Disaster Management Plan 2025-26 lists the places where water collects in heavy rain by name, fire station by fire station, without locations, so they cannot be placed in wards.

drainage._data_status_note: We have not found NMC's storm-water drains published as a map or a file. The City Development Plan 2041 (March 2015) puts the network at about 917 km, as surveyed in 2008.

sewerage._data_status_note: NMC's Environment Status Report 2023-24 locates its sewage treatment plants, but we have not found a map of the sewer network, so sewer lines cannot be placed in wards.

industrial._data_status_note: MPCB's river action plans name the power stations and industries along the Kanhan and the Kolar, but we have not found their locations published, so they cannot be placed in wards.

block.name: Nagpur (Urban)
block.note: In IN-GRES's 2023-2024 area figures Nagpur (Urban) first appears with 22,457 ha, and three units' assessed areas fall by the same total: Nagpur (Rural) by 6,277 ha, Kamptee by 16,081 ha (all of it canal command area) and Hingna by 99 ha. The 2025-2026 row enters 206 ha of the unit's 22,457 ha as canal command area (16,081 ha the year before); its other figures repeat the 2024-2025 non-command values, so the stage, 54.62%, is in effect that of the non-command part alone (33.10% for the whole unit the year before). The category, Safe in all three editions, is the steadier comparison.
